title: How do we write a number given in words using figures?
description: The video turns four numbers given in words into figures with Indian commas, group by group, and shows where a zero must fill an empty place. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that four lakh seven thousand seven hundred four is forty seven thousand seven hundred four.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number in words is written as groups, with two digits in the thousands group and three in the last group, so empty places are filled with zeros. Ask the class how many digits each group must have before anyone writes. Watch for students who write seven thousand as a single digit and so lose a zero.

source: Write in digits: (a) one lakh twenty three thousand four hundred and fifty six, (b) four lakh seven thousand seven hundred and four, (c) fifty lakhs five thousand and fifty, (d) ten lakhs two hundred and thirty five
video_script.why: The child can read big numbers in words and knows how the commas split them into groups.
video_script.substitution: A number in words is written group by group: the thousands group has two digits and the last group has three, so empty places are filled with zeros.
video_script.anchor: Write in digits: one lakh twenty three thousand four hundred fifty six, and three more numbers said in words
video_script.wrong_answer: forty seven thousand seven hundred four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes four lakh seven thousand seven hundred four as four, seven, seven hundred four with no zero. Seven thousand sits in a two digit thousands group, so a zero is needed before the seven.
video_script.payoff_line: Ten lakh two hundred thirty five has two zeros in the middle group

final_answer.spoken: ten lakh two hundred thirty five

never_show: a number with a crore group
maths_rules: the slip: 4,7,704 read as 47,704, forty seven thousand seven hundred four
video_script.design: One idea: write a number in words group by group; the thousands group has two digits and the last group has three. Wrong idea: Keeko drops the zero in the thousands group. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the second number is forty seven thousand seven hundred four. It wrote four, seven, seven hundred four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But the thousands group has two digits, so seven thousand is written zero seven. That keeps the four in the lakh place.
